newsitem.title: KENYA: Financials sustain upbeat Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Financials sustain upbeat Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Strong demand for financials sustained the bullish profile of the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Tuesday, brokers and bourse officials said.
"Investors are buying heavily in the financials because they're expecting some good dividends with the end-results to come soon," one broker said.
The index gained 18.46 points to stand at 3279.51. Turnover was posted at 21.649 million shillings traded on 384,363 shares from 22.304 million shillings traded on 359,105 shares.

Kenya Commercial Bank traded 131,000 shares at a reserve price of 85 from 80 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 56 from 53.50. Barclays Bank gained 3.0 to close at 113, while National Bank of Kenya traded at 16.10 from 16.75.
Kenya Power & Lighting jumped to 176 from 170 while oil concern Total Kenya closed at 70 from 67.50.
Brokers and bourse officials said there had been a lot of support for the power monopoly share from institutional investors and more recently foreign investors.

"There is a lot of goodwill from institutional investors for the share, while foreign investors have been known to traditionally invest in utilities because their demand will never dwindle," a senior broker said.
A bourse official said underselling in Brooke Bond depressed the price to 154 from 170. Rea Vipingo eased to 10.60 from 10.75 while Sasini Tea & Coffee gained 50 cents to close at 64.50.
In the commercials Uchumi Supermarket closed at 55 unchanged while Kenya Airways gained five cents to 9.75.
